a.title: ASG survey of student activity preferences
a.body: The Associated Students published a survey of what activities students wanted, reported by Ellen Bennett in the same issue as a Herald piece commending the government's efforts and coverage of the Kentucky Intercollegiate Press Association backing a proposal for student representation.

b.title: Associated Students survey students on activity preferences
b.body: The Herald reported the results of an Associated Students survey under the headline "Associated Students' Survey Reveals Activity Preferences." The same issue carried a letter headed "Commends Associated Student Government's Efforts."

a.title: ASG rescues the Student Volunteer Bureau
a.body: ASG agreed to administer the Student Volunteer Bureau. The Herald reported that the bureau was rescued by the student government's action.

b.title: Volunteer Bureau and tutorial programme absorbed into ASG
b.body: The Student Volunteer Bureau, which placed students in community volunteer work, was weakened when founder Rodney Berry could not secure administrators or funds. Berry approached president Jeff Consolo about folding it into ASG, and the merger passed at the last meeting of the fall semester by better than 80 per cent; the tutorial programme was consolidated into ASG at the same time.

a.title: Judicial Council denies Johnson's appeal
a.body: After a long debate, the Associated Student Government Judicial Council denied Ed Johnson's appeal of the election result, letting Steve Thornton's win stand.

b.title: Judicial council denies election appeal
b.body: After losing candidate Ed Johnson contested the election result, the ASG judicial council denied his appeal following a long debate. The Herald had criticized the appeal system's lack of objectivity while the case was pending.

a.title: Jack Smith ends his term
a.body: The Herald marked the end of Jack Smith's presidency with a news story, an editorial crediting his enthusiasm with reviving interest in ASG, and an editorial cartoon. Mitchell McKinney had been elected the new president the week before.

b.title: Jack Smith ended his term as ASG president
b.body: Mack Humphreys reported on Jack Smith finishing his run as Associated Student Government president. A companion article in the same issue said Smith's enthusiasm had revived student interest in ASG, and Kevin Knapp drew an editorial cartoon on Smith and the organisation.

a.title: An extra study day recommended
a.body: ASG recommended adding an extra study day before exams. The proposal followed January efforts to find a way to print teacher evaluations.

b.title: ASG recommended an extra study day
b.body: Diane Tsimekles reported that Associated Student Government recommended adding an extra study day to the university calendar. The recommendation was carried in the Herald's 16 February issue.

a.title: ASG bill funds renovation of its own chambers
a.body: The Associated Student Government introduced Bill #91-03-F, providing for the renovation of the ASG chambers.

b.title: ASG bill proposes changing its own slogan
b.body: The Associated Student Government introduced Bill #91-11-F, proposing to change the organization's slogan, in the same fall that it voted to rename itself from the Associated Students to the Student Government Association.

a.title: A coffee house for Pride Week and a Homecoming float
a.body: In a single October session the congress passed Bill 98-5-F funding a coffee house for Pride Week and Bill 98-6-F funding a joint SGA and Hillraiser Homecoming float. The fall slate also included a W.O.W. conference, ashtrays outside residence halls and an SGA survey.

b.title: Pride Week coffee house in Niteclass
b.body: SGA co-sponsored a coffee house with the African-American Players on Thursday 5 November 1998 at 9.30 p.m. in Niteclass, to mark Pride Week. Bill 98-5-F described it as a place for students to share their creative talents and as the academic component of the week.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 98-5-F, Coffee House for Pride Week

a.title: Disputed 9-8 vote clouds the first speaker of the senate election
a.body: Congress elected constitution author Robert Watkins as the first speaker of the senate by 9 votes to 8 over Brittany Fausey, with 17 of 20 members present voting. The result was immediately questioned because the new constitution was unclear on whether two-thirds of eligible voters or of total membership was required, and three members present were barred from voting under a judicial council ruling. Martin warned of a "semester of frustration" if the dispute was not resolved at the year's final meeting, while Fausey declined to challenge the result.

b.title: Turnout questions cloud election of first senate speaker
b.body: SGA congress elected Bowling Green sophomore Robert Watkins as speaker of the senate, a position created under the new constitution. The Herald reported that the number of voters who participated might not be sufficient to uphold the decision.

a.title: SGA pays surprise $15,000 bill for previous year's Provide-A-Ride
a.body: SGA paid Parking Services a $15,000 retroactive payment for the prior year's Provide-A-Ride service after Parking Services found no record of the previous administration's payment. The money was split evenly between the organizational aid and student scholarship funds, $7,500 from each. Stephens said he was "shocked" by the bill, while 2010-11 president Colton Jessie insisted his administration had budgeted the money.

b.title: SGA pays $15,000 retroactive Provide-A-Ride bill from aid and scholarship funds
b.body: SGA paid Parking Services a $15,000 retroactive payment for the previous year's Provide-A-Ride service, taking $7,500 each from the organizational aid and student scholarship funds. President Billy Stephens said he was "shocked" to be notified of the payment the week before, and that Parking Services had not received the money from the previous administration. Because the SGA budget does not roll over between years, no prior-year funds were available to cover it.

a.title: SGA passed its teaching assistant evaluation resolution
a.body: On Feb. 5 the senate passed a resolution creating teaching assistant evaluations, a program Dodds had campaigned on and drafted with his executive officers to pitch to Provost Gordon Emslie. Nicki Seay, chair of the Legislative Research Committee, wrote the bill, which aimed to make TA evaluation uniform across departments. The resolution next needed review by the Academic Quality Committee and approval by the University Senate.

b.title: Teaching assistant evaluation resolution clears the senate
b.body: The senate passed a resolution for teaching assistant evaluations on Feb. 5, a proposal President Cory Dodds had campaigned on and developed with the executive officers before pitching it to Provost Gordon Emslie. The resolution next had to be reviewed by the Academic Quality Committee and, if endorsed, approved by the University Senate. Dodds said the idea had been worked on for many years.

a.title: Fall election drew 564 voters, created international seat
a.body: A total of 564 voters cast ballots in the fall SGA election. A referendum creating the Navitas/ESL international student senate seat passed with 310 of 426 votes, or 73 percent. Six freshman senators were elected out of seven candidates, with Jay Todd Richey taking 27 percent of the vote, and most college senate seats went to unopposed candidates.

b.title: 564 vote in fall election; referendum creates the Navitas/ESL seat
b.body: A total of 564 students voted in the fall election. The referendum creating a Navitas and English as a Second Language international student senate seat drew 426 votes and passed with 310 yes votes, 73 percent. Six freshman senators were elected out of seven candidates, led by Jay Todd Richey with 27 percent, along with two graduate senators, a Gatton Academy senator and an Arts and Letters senator.

a.title: Herald editorial faulted SGA over registration policy
a.body: A Herald editorial accused SGA of failing to represent students on the new priority-registration hour cap, saying executive vice president Mark Reeves voted for the policy at University Senate on Sept. 10 without SGA questioning or debating it first. The editorial argued SGA had one job, representing students, and had not done it on this issue.

b.title: Herald editorial says SGA failed students on priority registration
b.body: A Herald editorial criticized SGA for scheduling an open forum on the new priority registration policy for Nov. 12, after the policy was already set to govern fall registration. The policy limited students with priority registration to 16 hours on their priority day, excluding seniors and graduate students. The editorial said SGA had missed the chance to represent students on an exclusively student issue, pointing to failures at a Sept. 10 meeting.

a.title: Senate defeated a nonsectarian prayer policy resolution
a.body: After more than 20 minutes of debate, the senate defeated Resolution 4-14-F, which would have supported adopting the University Senate's nonsectarian public prayer policy for university-sponsored events. President Nicki Taylor said the senate was split three ways among nonsectarian prayer, sectarian prayer and no prayer at all. The same night, senators passed Bill 9-14-F allocating $250 in organizational aid to the Phi Gamma Delta fraternity.

b.title: Senate defeats the nonsectarian prayer policy resolution
b.body: After more than 20 minutes of debate the senate defeated Resolution 4-14-F, which would have supported adopting the University Senate's nonsectarian public prayer policy for university-sponsored events. Chief of Staff Seth Church explained that a nonsectarian prayer differs from a sectarian one that refers to a specific deity. President Nicki Taylor said the senate was divided, which caused the resolution to be voted down.

a.title: SGA backed a $10 million parking garage funded by a $30 fee
a.body: SGA passed a resolution supporting construction of a new parking structure on part of Creason Lot, funded by a $30-per-semester tuition increase. Authors Zach Jones, Brian Chism and Nathan Cherry estimated the roughly 500-car garage would take about 18 months to build. Chief of Staff Seth Church objected that the plan was rushed and left out regional campuses.

b.title: SGA endorses a $10 million parking garage funded by a $30 tuition rise
b.body: SGA passed a resolution supporting a new parking structure funded by a $30 increase in tuition each semester. The resolution placed the garage on part of Creason Lot and suggested a temporary gravel lot on the site of Tate Page Hall after its anticipated demolition. President Nicki Taylor said the structure had been before the parking and transportation committee for the whole academic year, and the authors were Zach Jones, Brian Chism and Nathan Cherry.

a.title: Administration overrode student vote on pub name
a.body: Richey announced that administrators had renamed the future Garrett Conference Center pub "Topper Grill and Pub," setting aside the name students chose in SGA's "Dub the Pub" contest, Topper Tavern. Richey said Ransdell wanted to downplay the alcohol theme and called himself "very disappointed," saying the move made SGA question how much the administration listened to students. At the same meeting SGA introduced the RAVE Guardian campus safety app.

b.title: Administration overrides student vote on pub name
b.body: Richey announced that administrators had changed the winning pub name from Topper Tavern and Grill to Topper Grill and Pub, a decision he said was made by former Student Affairs Vice President Howard Bailey and reflected Ransdell's wish to downplay the alcohol theme. "I was very disappointed," Richey said, adding that it made SGA question how much the administration listens to students. The same meeting introduced the RAVE Guardian campus safety app.

a.title: SGA passes resolution supporting DACA students
a.body: At its Nov. 7 meeting the senate passed a resolution, co-authored by President Andi Dahmer and Francisco Serrano, standing in solidarity with WKU students who were DACA recipients. The measure passed 32-1 and was a revision of the clean DREAM Act resolution rejected the previous week, reframed to address only the WKU student community. Dahmer noted WKU was one of the last Kentucky schools to pass something of this nature.

b.title: Narrower DACA solidarity resolution passes 32-1
b.body: Two weeks after the DREAM Act resolution failed, a rewritten resolution by Dahmer and Francisco Serrano declaring SGA's solidarity with WKU students who are DACA recipients passed 32-1. Dahmer said the new version stayed within "a jurisdiction that we do have" rather than calling on legislators. The same meeting unanimously funded the Go With the Flow program, allocating over $580 for free menstrual products in five campus buildings.

a.title: Transparency resolution passed after the dean's resignation
a.body: A week after Snyder's sudden resignation, the senate passed Resolution 4-19-S by a 30-2 vote, calling on top university officials to provide explanations for major decisions. In the same meeting it rejected Mayer's Judicial Council nominee Wood Brown 17-11, created a senate seat for first-generation college students 33-0, and passed a resolution 33-0 asking WKU to let students' preferred names appear on class rosters, IDs and email addresses, a measure brought by the Transgender Non-Binary student organization.

b.title: Senate demands administrative transparency after a dean's sudden resignation
b.body: Resolution 4-19-S, passed 30-2 a week after Potter College Dean Larry Snyder resigned abruptly, said top university officials must explain such decisions and implement them in a manner that protects the dignity of those involved. Mayer's renomination of Wood Brown to the Judicial Council was struck down 17-11, short of two-thirds, after Associate Justice Annalicia Carlson said the council preferred Erika Puhakka. A bill creating a first-generation senate seat and a resolution on transgender students' preferred names each passed 33-0.

a.title: Executive board veto of Resolution 4-19-F upheld
a.body: The executive board vetoed Resolution 4-19-F by a 4-0 vote with two abstentions, and the senate confirmed the veto at its Tuesday meeting. President Will Harris, one of the abstainers, said the resolution's discrimination claim would have to come from the Student Code of Conduct and no violation had been noted by the Office of Student Conduct, while co-author Anthony Survance accused the executive branch of dragging the issue out. Senators also raised Harris's connection to Alpha Xi Delta as one of its knights, which he rejected as grounds for bias.

b.title: Executive board vetoes Resolution 4-19-F 4-0; senate sustains the veto
b.body: The executive board vetoed the Alpha Xi Delta resolution 4-0 with two of six members abstaining, and the senate confirmed the veto. President Will Harris, who abstained, said the discrimination clause the resolution invoked would have to come from the Student Code of Conduct and that the Office of Student Conduct had noted no violation. Legislative Research Chair Josh Zaczek disputed the reasoning, and Harris was questioned about his status as an Alpha Xi Delta knight.

a.title: Associate provost rebuffed SGA's P/D/F request; computers bill passes 28-3
a.body: Edmonds told senators that Associate Provost Rob Hale had defended the university's decision to extend the drop deadline rather than restore Pass/D/Fail grading, and said he was "deeply disturbed" by the response; senator Brenna Mathews argued the policy left students choosing between attending in person or paying for an extra semester. Edmonds urged senators to keep circulating his petition, which had passed 3,000 signatures, and the senate voted 28-3 to fund recycled computers for the SGA office, a number scaled back to meet CDC guidelines.

b.title: Provost's office rejects SGA's Pass/D/Fail request; petition passes 3,000 signatures
b.body: Associate Provost Rob Hale defended the university's decision to extend the class drop deadline instead of restoring Pass/D/Fail. President Garrett Edmonds said he was "deeply disturbed" and urged senators to email the Faculty Senate and the provost, noting his petition had passed 3,000 signatures. The senate separately passed a bill funding recycled computers for the SGA office 28-3, with the number reduced to comply with CDC guidance.

a.title: A Title IX report seeks the President's removal
a.body: Filed with Student Conduct. Under the constitution, removing an executive who will not resign requires written endorsement from at least 20% of the Senate, a wait of at least fourteen days and a two-thirds vote of the full Senate sitting as a court.

b.title: Title IX complaint against SGA president seeks his removal
b.body: A Title IX report filed Feb. 19 accused President Cole Bornefeld, described in the report as student regent and representative of the student body, of gender-based harassment over four Turning Point USA Instagram posts he liked. The complaint sought his removal, a public statement from WKU and a public apology; the complainant's identity was redacted from records released to the Herald. Spokesperson Jace Lux said WKU does not comment on Student Conduct complaints, and the Herald noted removal would require impeachment endorsed by 20% of the senate and a two-thirds vote.

a.title: Election reform bill failed 19-15
a.body: Bill 39-23-S, which would have moved the transfer, non-traditional and first-generation senate seats to the fall election and required a two-thirds senate vote to convert vacant seats to at-large seats, failed 19-15, short of the two-thirds needed. Sponsor Neel Patel called the growing reliance on presidential appointments a dangerous practice for a government organization. The same meeting unanimously funded the April 3 Afro-Latinidad cultural event and rejected funding for Dance Big Red.

b.title: Election reform bill fails 19-15; Dance Big Red funding rejected
b.body: Bill 39-23-S, which would have moved transfer, non-traditional and first-generation senate seats to the fall election and required a two-thirds senate vote before a vacant seat could become an at-large seat, failed 19-15 because it did not reach the required two-thirds. Gatton Academy Senator Neel Patel said reliance on the president to convert vacancies was a dangerous practice for a government organization. Bill 41-23-S, funding Dance Big Red, also failed, while Bill 40-23-S funding an Afro-Latinidad event passed unanimously.

a.title: Uber voucher program and parking fee measures
a.body: President Sam Kurtz and Chief of Staff Donte Reed announced a program of 450 Uber vouchers worth $10 each, distributed through social media giveaways, meeting attendance and SGA events. The senate also passed Resolution 18-23-S supporting a cap on student parking fees at $50 and Bill 19-23-S allocating $700 to help financially vulnerable students pay parking fines, along with $1,045 in Dental Hygiene Center and ID Center vouchers.

b.title: SGA launches Uber voucher program and moves against parking fees
b.body: Kurtz and Chief of Staff Donte Reed announced 450 Uber vouchers worth $10 each, distributed through social media giveaways, meeting attendance and need-based scholarships. Resolution 18-23-S, written by Denney and Reed, put SGA on record supporting a $50 cap on student parking fees, noting citations ranged from $10 to $600. Bill 19-23-S set aside $700 to pay citations for financially vulnerable students, excluding tickets for disability, safety zone or fire lane violations.

a.title: Senate revived the transcript voucher program
a.body: The senate passed Bill 24-25-F, authored by Legislative Operations Committee Chair Caden Lucas, allocating $195 to reestablish the transcript voucher program, giving students one free official transcript a semester. It also funded a new "Professor of the Month" award and ping pong equipment for the DSU recreation area.

b.title: Transcript voucher program reestablished
b.body: Bill 24-25-F, introduced by Legislative Operations Committee Chair Caden Lucas, allocated $195 from the legislative discretionary fund for 15 transcript vouchers distributed at the SGA office, one per student per semester. Lucas said WKU charges $13 to send a single transcript and that the cost stacks. The meeting also funded a Professor of the Month award and replacement ping pong equipment for the DSU recreation area.
